title: Nonlocal Magic Spreading in Many-body Quantum Dynamics: From Chaotic Evolution to Quasi-particle Picture in Integrable Models
authors: Sreemayee Aditya, Piotr Sierant, Xhek Turkeshi
abstract: Entanglement and magic are resources that reveal complementary aspects of quantum many-body systems. Their interplay is captured by nonlocal magic, the magic that survives arbitrary local changes of basis. Yet their markedly different dynamical behavior leaves open how this irreducible component of magic spreads. Here we connect nonlocal magic to the capacity of entanglement, a tractable quantity measuring fluctuations of the entanglement Hamiltonian. This connection enables analytically controlled predictions across a wide range of many-body dynamics, from chaotic to integrable systems, which we investigate also using large-scale numerical simulations. In chaotic systems, nonlocal magic exhibits a transient buildup, with logarithmic growth in time followed by decay to a size-independent value. For integrable systems, we develop a quasiparticle picture in quantitative agreement with numerics, showing that the same initial growth instead leads to saturation at a value logarithmic in subsystem size. These contrasting behaviors have an operational consequence for entanglement embezzlement: the strongest scramblers embezzle only transiently, whereas free-fermionic dynamics can sustain universal embezzlement in the steady state.
summary: This work explores the spreading of 'nonlocal magic,' a measure of quantum resource, by linking it to the capacity of entanglement. The authors find that chaotic systems show transient buildup of this magic, while integrable systems sustain a steady-state value proportional to the subsystem size. This reveals fundamental differences in how quantum information is scrambled or preserved in different physical models.
main_problem: The paper investigates how 'nonlocal magic,' a resource quantifying magic surviving local basis changes, spreads across different quantum many-body dynamics.
main_result: Nonlocal magic exhibits transient logarithmic growth followed by decay in chaotic systems, but saturates at a value proportional to the subsystem size logarithm in integrable (free-fermionic) systems.
method: The authors connect nonlocal magic to the capacity of entanglement, using Gaussian approximations and comparing results across different dynamical regimes.
model_or_system: The study analyzes many-body quantum systems using models ranging from chaotic dynamics (e.g., Haar random circuits) to integrable systems (e.g., free-fermionic Hamiltonians).
key_observables: Nonlocal Magic (DNL), Capacity of Entanglement (C), and Entanglement Entropy (S).
important_parameters: Time ($t$), subsystem size ($L_A$), and the distinction between chaotic vs. integrable dynamics.
main_assumptions: The initial analysis relies on the Gaussian approximation for Schmidt sums, which is controlled when higher normalized cumulants are small.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares DNL evolution for ergodic vs. free-fermionic dynamics, showing $\log t 	o \mathcal{O}(1)$ vs. $\log t 	o \log^2 L_A$. Figure 2 shows the rise-peak-fall profile of capacity in random circuits.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the connection between nonlocal magic and entanglement capacity, then analyzes the time evolution of this quantity across chaotic, integrable, and quasi-equilibrium systems, concluding with operational consequences for entanglement embezzlement.
why_interesting: The contrast between transient scrambling in chaotic systems and sustained, universal embezzlement in integrable systems provides a deep, quantifiable diagnostic tool for characterizing the underlying dynamics of complex quantum matter.
